output.brief: The Android login drop is most likely caused by a vendor rule update at the edge, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane activated a new rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks password requests from the networking library our Android app uses, returning HTTP 403. Failures began at 10:41 on every app version at once, including versions without the new library. About 41,300 devices were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. The OS security patch makes no difference, and 6.14 is only 5% of traffic, so a rollback would not fix this. Credential-stuffing is not the cause, and it would not show up in the telemetry anyway. I'm fairly confident in this. Next steps: ask Corvane today to set that rule to log-only on the password-login path, keeping rate limits, lockout and all other rules. Then check that Android password success returns to about 96%. Don't raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Let the 6.14 rollout continue while you track outcomes by version. Also ask for vendor rule changes to be tested before they go live.
